g.text: One repository, so one commit fixes every byte of every artifact
the cargo workspace, the C shim and the Vx code side by side · §1.2
pinned rustc, plus rustfmt, clippy, miri, llvm-tools
cargo-deny: licenses, advisories, bans, duplicate versions
the only modules allowed to contain `unsafe` (§3.2), with owners
hot symbols and the callees they must not contain (§4.4)
owners for UNSAFE.toml modules, c/, vx/, supply-chain/
crates under INV-DET; they share the strict clippy.toml below
bans floats, std::time, RandomState, logging, threads (§3.3)
Rust side of the NIC; links c/vyrn-nic-shim on Linux
binary-only packages: main.rs + config wiring, no logic
the C ABI that vyrn-nic binds
pinned ef_vi and DPDK headers, one directory per vendor release
vxc v0.0.4, commit 3a89e3c7; the hash of the vxc binary
the only way Vx artifacts are built (§5.4)
every Vx workaround, each naming its vx-lang/Vx issue (§5.6)
C ABI shared by Rust and Vx: structs, rings, entry points
cargo-fuzz package (outside the workspace) and corpora (§6.6)
wire, SipHash, BLAKE3, LEB128 vectors; golden responses
golden order-stream logs with expected output hashes
vyrn-sim seeds that once failed; each runs on every commit
generator configs; each names a 02 workload ID
per-runner baselines for the perf gate (§9.3)
signed benchmark reports, one per run that gates something
config schema, versioned with the protocol (§10.1)
reproducible OS image recipe (kernel cmdline per 06)
one commit hash per release: every box prints the same one
